text:
Pooled token residuals are cheap but permutation-invariant: identical token multisets cannot distinguish “USB-C to HDMI” from “HDMI to USB-C,” or reliably bind multiple numbers to units. Distinct model/format tokens can survive pooling if tokenization preserves them. [Deep averaging networks](https://aclanthology.org/P15-1162/) demonstrate useful unordered representations; [small CNNs](https://aclanthology.org/D14-1181/) provide ordered local filters. Neither establishes attribute-level superiority for scratch-trained HSTU recommendation. A width-2/3/5 CNN is a plausible lightweight extension for local relations; reliable connector direction spanning longer text may require larger receptive fields or a small GRU. These are architectural inferences, not measured benchmark gains.

Reproducible experimental choices: preserve digits, decimals, hyphens, slashes and direction words; retain “3.5mm,” “USB-C,” “DVD-Audio,” and model identifiers; separate title/description fields; fix truncation lengths. Build vocabulary from permitted metadata with deterministic frequency/lexical ordering; reserve PAD/UNK and add character n-grams for rare identifiers, following the mechanism in [subword embeddings](https://aclanthology.org/Q17-1010/), with all parameters trained from scratch. Compare masked mean pooling against the CNN using identical tokenization. Proposed fusion: e_item + sigmoid(g)·LayerNorm(project(text)), initialize g=-3, and force the residual to zero for missing text. Mask padding throughout pooling and convolution. These gating/normalization settings are proposed defaults, not literature-established optima; serialize vocabulary and preprocessing with the checkpoint.

[HDCCF](https://ijcai.org/proceedings/2022/327) documents the recommendation trade-off between informative hard negatives and false negatives, but does not establish a false-negative rate for title-neighbor sampling here. Similar products may be unobserved positives. Exclude known training positives, compare uniform sampling with a small neighbor fraction, and select using fixed validation HR@10.
